verdict:
CONDITIONAL YES (INFERRED, about 65-75% for the full outcome). A real Chromium can show live runoff coverage on a Web Displays-style multiblock telão at spawn on the GTNH 1.7.10 server on Sun 2026-10-25, if all of the following hold.

(1) Platforms. The browser runs client-side and in-process. It uses our own build of CCBlueX java-cef (BSD), compiled to Java 8 bytecode. Supported clients are Windows 10/11 x64 (Tier 1) and Linux x64 (Tier 2), on the GTNH version the server freezes, on both Java 8 and Java 17-25 (lwjgl3ify), with Angelica on. Any other client (macOS, arm64, Win7/8.1, Pojav, or a failed install) sees a labelled placeholder and keeps playing. It does not crash.

(2) Video source. The live video reaches the screen as a page we control on an Akashic HTTPS domain. The primary path is the Akashic relay: OBS/ffmpeg -> MediaMTX -> WebRTC (WHEP), with LL-HLS as fallback, carrying VP9 (or AV1) plus Opus. Measured on localhost inside JCEF/Chromium 150: 126 ms added delay over WebRTC and about 1.04 s over LL-HLS (VERIFIED, codec-path). These codecs need no proprietary CEF build. The backup path uses the same engine built against OBS's codec-enabled CEF 150 (7871), so an official YouTube embed (H.264/AAC) plays in each client. That build ran H.264/AAC, MSE TS, native HLS and WebRTC on Linux (VERIFIED). It has not been run on Windows: gate G1.

(3) Rights. A source with retransmission rights (for the relay) or an embeddable YouTube source (for the backup) is chosen by Wed 10-21. Rights are the owner's call. Neither path is legal by default (Lei 9.610 art. 95; YouTube ToS forbids restreaming but allows the embed).

(4) Scope. The work is cut to a telão-only MVP: an admin-locked screen block, URL presets, live-edge/clock sync and distance volume. No minePad, laser, peripherals, upgrades, JS API or miniserv before the event.

(5) Gates. G1-G6 below pass on their dates. Staffing: the estimate is 16-28 person-days in 15 calendar days (INFERRED), so this needs two parallel streams (engine+relay, and the WD port) or the owner accepts a smaller MVP.

What it will NOT be: "almost 0 ms" behind the real event. The broadcaster's and YouTube's delay (seconds) cannot be removed. What it can be: players within tens of ms of each other (WebRTC), or under about 100-250 ms (LL-HLS with server-clock steering, INFERRED, gate G4).

Labelled safety nets, in order. SN1: the same in-game browser loads TSE's official results web page (a real web page, no video codecs needed). SN2: for clients without CEF, an AkashicFM radio relay of the coverage audio, only if rights allow. SN3: a static poster.

Evidence status: nothing has been built or run inside Minecraft yet. Every in-game claim below is INFERRED until gates G1-G3.
architecture:
Each part below carries its evidence grade.

1. ENGINE (which JCEF build).
- Base: CCBlueX/java-cef, pinned commit (fe8cc9e was the one tested), BSD.
- Why this base:
  - It is already on CEF 152 (VERIFIED).
  - It has no AWT/JOGL dependency.
  - N_DoMessageLoopWork is public and pumping is left to the game.
  - It has CefAudioHandler, for stage-2 audio.
- Rejected alternatives:
  - Upstream/jcefmaven: needs the AWT EDT and has no audio handler (VERIFIED).
  - CinemaMod: Chromium 116, Java 21/GLFW only, --disable-web-security (VERIFIED). Kept only as an emergency fallback; its hosted natives do decode H.264/AAC (VERIFIED).
  - montoyo MCEF 1.7.10: 2015 CEF, usr_paths hack fails on Java 9+ (VERIFIED).
- Build: we fork CCBlueX's build-jcef.yml and build only windows-amd64 and linux-amd64. Each platform's libjcef is linked against the exact CEF distribution it ships with, because java-cef uses CEF's unversioned experimental API (VERIFIED).
- Two variants from one workflow, selected by a build flag:
  - (a) PRIMARY: OBS CEF 7871 (150.0.20 Windows / 150.0.19 Linux), codec-enabled, SHA-256 pinned as in OBS CMakePresets.json:54-66. Needs a 6-line #if guard in jni_util.cpp for 3 missing net error codes. Built and run on Linux in about 5 minutes (VERIFIED). Windows is untested (gate G1).
  - (b) ALTERNATE: Spotify/jcefbuild CEF 152.0.6, codec-free. Used if the owner rejects codec distribution or the OBS build fails on Windows. Path D still works on it, because VP8/VP9/AV1/Opus are always built (VERIFIED from Chromium gni files). The runtime test on this build is still pending (INFERRED, gate G1).
- Small native patches in the same build:
  - (i) Plain-int JNI entry points for key, mouse and wheel input. The fork's input code looks up org/lwjgl/sdl classes that do not exist on Java 8 or lwjgl3ify 2.x (VERIFIED).
  - (ii) Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, plus a uniquely named helper exe (akashicweb_helper), so orphan cleanup only ever targets our own helpers.
  - (iii) Stage-2 only: audio_handler.cpp uses JCEF's cached-loader FindClass and reads back the audio params.
- Java side:
  - jcef classes compiled with --release 8 (class major 52), unrelocated, because JNI symbols are bound to org.cef names (VERIFIED).
  - Our own OSR class in package org.cef.browser, a pattern proven with no JOGL (VERIFIED).
  - DataPointer falls back to a reflective DirectByteBuffer.
  - On startup, refuse with a clear message if another mod already loaded org.cef.
- CEF threading: a dedicated daemon thread "AkashicWeb-Pump" runs CefApp init and the external message pump. onPaint copies the dirty rects into a triple buffer; the probe measured 0.85-1.14 ms per 1080p frame (VERIFIED). The render thread then uploads the newest frame.
- CEF switches: --no-first-run (startup fails without it in the probe, VERIFIED), --no-default-browser-check, --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required.
  - NEVER --disable-web-security.
  - Popups, downloads, devtools, remote debugging and the context menu are disabled.
- Profile: a per-instance root_cache_path under <gameDir>/akashic-web/profile, because of the CEF singleton lock (VERIFIED).
- Browser settings: windowless_frame_rate 30, telão browser fixed at 1280x720. A client preset can drop to 480p or Off.
- In-process vs separate host process: in-process for the MVP, because it is the proven MCEF pattern and there is no time for an IPC layer. A separate browser-host process (shared-memory frames, supervisor) is post-election work.

2. MOD STRUCTURE.
- A new GTNH-buildscript mod, e.g. modid 'akashicwd', named as a Web Displays port with montoyo's public-domain credit and the CinemaMod MIT notice where fork code is borrowed.
- Compiled with Jabel to class major 52, with a CI check that every class is major 52.
- Packages:
  - common: BlockScreen, Multiblock, BlockSide, hit2pixels, Rotation, TileEntityScreen with NBT and the telão lock, ScreenRights, the network subset.
  - server: /telao command, policy, audit, rate limits.
  - client: TESR, upload, GUIs, input mapping.
  - client.web: the ONLY package that touches org.cef, so the dedicated server never loads natives (VERIFIED requirement from the issue history).
- Mixins via UniMixins: only a Minecraft.shutdown hook.
- Soft dependencies, all reflective:
  - Angelica: TileEntityRenderBoundsRegistry.registerDynamicClass.
  - lwjgl3ify 3.x: InputEvents.beginTextInput/endTextInput.
  - AkashicFM: clock and stage-2 audio.
- Not ported before the event: the JSON GUI framework, miniserv/server block/wd:// scheme (never: open TCP port), minePad, laser, peripherals, upgrades, JS/redstone API, advancements, ironic.ogg (never shipped).

3. RENDERING.
- The TESR only draws: one Tessellator quad, lightmap 240/240, lighting off, all exceptions caught with a placeholder drawn instead.
- Upload happens once per frame on RenderTickEvent START, outside the TESR, because Iris's shadow pass calls TESRs again (VERIFIED).
- The upload uses GL11/GL12 calls in our own (Angelica-redirected) classes:
  - texture allocated once as GL_RGBA8, LINEAR filtering, CLAMP, no mipmaps;
  - per dirty rect: set ROW_LENGTH/SKIP, glTexSubImage2D with GL_BGRA and GL_UNSIGNED_INT_8_8_8_8_REV, then reset all unpack state to 0, since Angelica beta66b does not track it (VERIFIED);
  - no PBOs in the MVP.
- getRenderBoundingBox returns the full multiblock AABB from the description packet, computed before the first render. The class is registered as a dynamic-bounds class with Angelica (VERIFIED requirement), and getMaxRenderDistanceSquared is raised to cover the plaza.
- The browser is hidden (wasHidden, uploads stop) when off-frustum or beyond the load range, and closed beyond the unload range with hysteresis.

4. INPUT (admin only).
- Server-side right-click goes through hit2pixels and a MOUSE_CLICK broadcast. CEF button numbering differs from LWJGL2 (1 and 2 swapped).
- Wheel deltas are normalised to notches x 120.
- The keyboard GUI sends RAWKEYDOWN/KEYUP with real modifiers through an LWJGL2 -> Windows VK table, and text as KEYEVENT_CHAR. SDL text input is switched on under lwjgl3ify 3.x. Paste is read on the sending client with GuiScreen.getClipboardString; copy and cut are never replicated.
- For the event, admins steer the screen through URL presets and commands, not in-world typing.

5. AUDIO.
- MVP: Chromium's own output, with volume set by our player page. Each tick the mod pushes a volume = distance gain (the curve from AkashicFM GainModel.sourceGain) x MC master x records. On pages that are not ours, the same value is applied by a generic script to every <video>/<audio>. Audio is muted and the browser closed on unload, world unload and disconnect.
- Stage 2 (post-election, or a stretch goal if green by 10-18): CefAudioHandler -> drop-oldest ring -> AkashicFM AudioFeed -> AudioEngine.touch with LEFT/RIGHT EmitterSpecs, OcclusionField and RoomProbe. CEF mutes the source while capturing (mute_source=true, VERIFIED in CEF source). This needs three AkashicFM changes first: an ExternalAudioSources API so RadioAudioController stops releasing the key, a non-blocking PcmRing, and a timed feed against lip-sync drift.

6. SYNC.
- Server-authoritative state: URL/preset, the source epoch, and a target delay D behind the live edge.
- All telão updates go to every player in the dimension, not the 64-block radius.
- Clock: the AkashicFM pattern (C2SClockPing/S2CClockPong -> ServerClock/ClockSync, VERIFIED classes). It is copied into the mod or used through the soft dependency, and the mod pushes serverNow into the page by executeJavaScript every second.
- The player page steers hls.js toward EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME (hls.playingDate) = serverNow - D, using playbackRate within ±5% and seeking if more than 1 s off (INFERRED design, gate G4).
- WebRTC is near-live by construction: 22 ms skew between two clients on localhost (VERIFIED).
- Navigation is locked: onBeforeBrowse cancels anything outside the allowlist and reloads the server URL. This removes the 'CANNOT be fixed' navigation FIXME for the telão.
- All packet sends go through main-thread queues, the AkashicFM ClientTaskQueue/ServerActionQueue pattern (VERIFIED requirement).

7. RELAY (primary codec path D).
- MediaMTX v1.21.1 runs on a VPS or the game host with at least 300 Mbit/s of egress. The owner's home link only uploads the ingest.
- Ingest: OBS on the owner's PC sends SRT/RTMP H.264+AAC.
  - Primary transcode: MediaMTX runOnAvailable runs ffmpeg libvpx-vp9 realtime 720p30 at 1.8 Mbit/s + libopus 128k. This is the exact measured pipeline: 0.40 core (VERIFIED). A 480p tier is also produced.
  - Alternate: OBS WHIP AV1+Opus direct, no transcode (VERIFIED as supported by OBS, not measured end to end).
- Delivery: WebRTC over WHEP, with a TCP fallback and webrtcAdditionalHosts set; LL-HLS over HTTPS :443 as automatic fallback.
- The player page is served from an Akashic HTTPS domain behind a reverse proxy.
- Backup path B: the same page in 'embed' mode (youtube-nocookie, with a Referer), on the codec build.

8. NATIVES DISTRIBUTION.
- A client-only CefNativesInstaller built from the AkashicFM ToolManager skeleton (VERIFIED class):
  - a manifest pinned in the jar (platform, url, size, sha256, buildId);
  - .part download with resume, timeouts and retries over a mirror list (GitHub Releases + Akashic host);
  - SHA-256 checked BEFORE extraction;
  - zip extraction with a canonical-path check;
  - size caps raised to 512 MiB per file and 1 GiB total (libcef.so is 267.9 MB, VERIFIED);
  - an atomic directory rename and a .complete marker;
  - hashes re-verified at startup;
  - installed to <mcDataDir>/akashic-web/<platform>/<buildId>, never mods/ and never relative to the working directory, with an ASCII-safe fallback path;
  - player consent asked before the download; a manually supplied zip is accepted if it passes the same hash check.
- The codec CEF payload is either downloaded on the player's machine from OBS's CDN with OBS's pinned hash (no mirroring by Akashic), or stripped and repackaged. The owner decides.
- Everything is pre-downloaded from 10-20 on. On event day nothing should need downloading.

9. SECURITY / ADMIN CONTROL.
- The telão lock sets friendRights = otherRights = NONE. SetURL, Click, Type, Resolution and Sync require an OP level or the Akashic admin list.
- The original dimension and 128-block checks are kept, plus per-player rate limits and length caps.
- Server-side AkashicFM UrlPolicy: an https allowlist and isInternal blocking. AuditLog records every action.
- Client-side, onBeforeBrowse/onBeforeResourceLoad block file://, chrome://, internal addresses and popups.
- The sandbox stays off because JCEF hard-codes no_sandbox (VERIFIED). The allowlist is the mitigation.

10. JAVA / PLATFORM SUPPORT.
- Tier 1: Windows 10/11 x64 on Java 8 (LWJGL2) and on Java 17-25 (lwjgl3ify), Angelica on, on the frozen GTNH version. The recommendation is 2.8.4 stable; 2.9.0 is still RC-2 (VERIFIED).
- Tier 2: Linux x64, glibc 2.31 or newer.
- Unsupported, with placeholder and SN2: macOS (lwjgl3ify forces headless AWT and runs the game off the main thread; INFERRED incompatible with CEF on macOS), arm64, Win7/8.1, Pojav, OpenJ9.
- The mod is required in the pack, because the block registry must match. The CEF natives are optional: a client without them joins and sees the placeholder.
- A login handshake reports java.version, lwjgl3ify version, OS, GPU and preflight result to the server, collected in the audit log.

problem_fixes.fix: On a locked telão, onBeforeBrowse cancels navigation outside the allowlist and reloads the server URL, and popups are blocked. On unlocked screens (post-event), the admin client reports navigation as a rate-limited SetURL queued on the main thread.

problem_fixes.problem: No playback sync between players / desync by design / hls.js picks its own live edge
problem_fixes.fix: Server-authoritative source epoch and target delay D. The AkashicFM clock ping-pong (ServerClock/ClockSync) offset is pushed to the page. The page steers hls.playingDate toward serverNow-D (playbackRate ±5%, seek if more than 1 s off). WebRTC is near-live by design. Gate G4 measures the skew.
problem_fixes.source: wd-code; issues (mcef#62, WD#44); codec-path (2-client 22 ms/116 ms measured); AkashicFM server/relay/ServerClock.java, client/relay/ClockSync.java

problem_fixes.problem: Late joiners miss clicks; unattended autoplay blocked
problem_fixes.fix: The telão starts itself: the player page autoplays (--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required), the URL and play state travel in the description packet, and a sync is sent on join. The design does not depend on clicks.

problem_fixes.problem: Update radius (64 blocks) smaller than useful view distance; short load/unload ranges restart video
problem_fixes.fix: Send telão updates to every player in the dimension. Per-screen load range with hysteresis; hide (wasHidden) instead of destroying the browser inside the plaza; destroy only beyond the unload range.

problem_fixes.problem: Audio not integrated with Minecraft (OS output, not positional, ignores volume sliders, YouTube-only JS volume)
problem_fixes.fix: MVP: our player page applies volume = distance gain (GainModel curve) x MC master x records, pushed every tick; a generic script does the same on any <video>/<audio>; mute and close on unload, world unload and disconnect. Positional OpenAL comes in stage 2.

problem_fixes.problem: No positional audio: upstream JCEF has no CefAudioHandler; fork audio WIP (~43 packets late)
problem_fixes.fix: Stage 2: CCBlueX CefAudioHandler -> drop-oldest ring -> AkashicFM AudioFeed -> AudioEngine.touch with EmitterSpec LEFT/RIGHT, OcclusionField and RoomProbe. CEF mutes the source while capturing.

problem_fixes.problem: Fork DataPointer requires LWJGL3 MemoryUtil (crashes on Java 8)
problem_fixes.fix: Our build of DataPointer uses MemoryUtil by reflection when it exists, otherwise a reflective DirectByteBuffer(long,int). Preferred long-term: a native NewDirectByteBuffer per channel.

problem_fixes.problem: audio_handler.cpp uses raw FindClass on the native audio thread (LaunchClassLoader classes invisible)
problem_fixes.fix: Patch it to use JCEF's cached-loader FindClass (jni_scoped_helpers). This patch is folded into the same native build as the input patch.

problem_fixes.problem: Audio parameters cannot be chosen from Java (null params, final fields)
problem_fixes.fix: Patch the native to read back the rate and layout and request 48 kHz stereo. Until then, resample with AkashicFM Resampler48k and downmix to stereo.

problem_fixes.problem: AkashicFM RadioAudioController releases foreign playback keys every tick (retainOnly/stopAll/DRY room)
problem_fixes.fix: Add an ExternalAudioSources.register(Provider) API to AkashicFM, merged into keep, occlusion and room. WD soft-depends on it.

problem_fixes.problem: Lip-sync drifts after a game hitch (~1 s OpenAL queue)
problem_fixes.fix: Timed feed: map CEF pts to ClockSync time with latency of about 120-150 ms, and delay video by a matching 4-5 frame ring. Only relevant once stage-2 audio exists.

problem_fixes.problem: PcmRing.write blocks the CEF audio thread
problem_fixes.fix: Use a non-blocking drop-oldest ring, copied synchronously inside the callback.

problem_fixes.problem: Angelica render-bounds cache culls the multiblock; no isGlobalRenderer in 1.7.10
problem_fixes.fix: getRenderBoundingBox returns the full multiblock AABB (or INFINITE for the telão) from the description packet before the first render. Reflective TileEntityRenderBoundsRegistry.registerDynamicClass, and a raised getMaxRenderDistanceSquared. Gate G3 checks it in-game.

problem_fixes.problem: GL state coherence/corruption under Angelica (immediate mode, untracked unpack/PBO state, shadow-pass double TESR)
problem_fixes.fix: Draw with Tessellator, not glBegin. Upload once per frame at RenderTickEvent START with GL11 in our own classes, resetting ROW_LENGTH/SKIP to 0, no PBO in the MVP. The TESR only draws.

problem_fixes.problem: Rendering issues: shaders darkening the screen, skewed/split frames, renderer exception hides the chunk, rainbow GL leak
problem_fixes.fix: Full-bright quad (lightmap 240). The texture is reallocated atomically on resize, and frames whose size does not match are dropped. Every TESR exception is caught and a placeholder drawn instead. Shaders are smoke-tested on and off with 2 packs.

problem_fixes.problem: Unsafe packet sending from non-main threads (SimpleNetworkWrapper shared attributes)
problem_fixes.fix: Every send goes through main-thread queues drained on Client/ServerTickEvent (AkashicFM ClientTaskQueue / ServerActionQueue pattern). Remove addScheduledTask.

problem_fixes.problem: Stock CEF has no H.264/AAC: YouTube live (AAC-only audio, H.264 HLS), Twitch and MP4 fail; white/black screens
problem_fixes.fix: PRIMARY: the Akashic relay converts to VP9 (or AV1) + Opus over WebRTC/LL-HLS. BACKUP: the engine built on OBS's codec CEF 7871 so a YouTube embed plays. Both are tested at G1 and G2.
problem_fixes.source: codec-path (yt-dlp#9043; relay measured 126 ms / 1.04 s); cef-tech probe; issues (WD#27, #114; CinemaMod/mcef#28)

problem_fixes.fix: Correct the shared notes: its hosted natives decode H.264/AAC (VERIFIED). Keep it only as an emergency fallback engine (Chromium 116, different fork API).

problem_fixes.fix: Build per platform against the exact OBS distribution, placed in third_party/cef with -DCEF_VERSION. Carry the 6-line jni_util.cpp guard. Pin OBS's SHA-256s. Run the Windows build at G1.

problem_fixes.fix: The relay path is royalty-free and primary. If the codec build is used: no Akashic mirror; download from OBS's CDN on the player's machine with a hash pin and a consent screen; documented as optional; the owner gets legal input. Decision by 10-13.

problem_fixes.problem: CEF profile singleton lock with multiple MC instances
problem_fixes.fix: Per-instance root_cache_path under <gameDir>/akashic-web/profile. On conflict, a PROFILE_LOCKED placeholder.

problem_fixes.problem: Browser lifecycle bugs: audio continues after breaking or leaving, duplicate browsers
problem_fixes.fix: A single BrowserRegistry keyed by screen id with ref-counting. Close on invalidate, chunk unload, world unload, disconnect and dimension change, plus a tick sweeper. Scripted tests for break, logout, rejoin and dimension hop.

problem_fixes.problem: Client crashes when the browser is unavailable (RuntimeException 'MCEF is missing')
problem_fixes.fix: Degrade gracefully to a placeholder texture with the reason code. Never throw on join.

problem_fixes.problem: Native crashes kill the game (in-process libcef)
problem_fixes.fix: MVP: Tier-1 platforms only, software compositing fallback, every native call guarded, crash reason recorded for the next start, automatic disable after 2 consecutive crashes. Post-event: a separate browser-host process with a supervisor.

problem_fixes.problem: GPU/OSR driver problems (white or black for one player)
problem_fixes.fix: OSR defaults to --disable-gpu-compositing, with a GPU toggle. GPU-process crash detection falls back to software. GPU and driver included in diagnostics.

problem_fixes.problem: Client cost: full-res upload and decode per player; CPU/RAM (0.54 GiB, 40% of a core at 1080p30 software)
problem_fixes.fix: Fixed 1280x720 at 30 fps, one shared browser per source, uploads paused when off-view or far, client presets Off/480p/720p, 8 GB RAM minimum documented. FPS measured at G3/G4.

problem_fixes.problem: Zero-copy accelerated paint not available (no upstream binding; EGL/EXT_memory_object not fit for 1.7.10)
problem_fixes.fix: CPU OnPaint path for the event. Accelerated paint as an opt-in on NVIDIA/Windows under lwjgl3ify later. PBO double-buffering after the event.

problem_fixes.problem: Frames delivered at Minecraft's FPS or blocking it
problem_fixes.fix: The dedicated pump thread decouples CEF from MC FPS. The render thread uploads only the newest frame.

problem_fixes.problem: Three different client stacks (Java8+LWJGL2; Java17+ lwjgl3ify 2.x GLFW + Angelica beta66b; lwjgl3ify 3.x SDL3 + Angelica 2.x core profile)
problem_fixes.fix: Freeze the server's GTNH version on 10-11 (recommended: 2.8.4). Test that version on Java 8 and Java 21. Detect lwjgl3ify 3.x reflectively. Add Angelica and lwjgl3ify to the AkashicFM tools/prod harness.

problem_fixes.problem: Direct LWJGL3 references renamed under lwjgl3ify (non-Aware jars)
problem_fixes.fix: The mod stays non-Aware. LWJGL3/lwjgl3ify APIs are reached only by reflection with string names.

problem_fixes.problem: Jabel/Java 8 API only (ProcessHandle etc. unavailable)
problem_fixes.fix: Java 9+ APIs via MethodHandles behind a version check. A CI gate that every class is major 52, including the org.cef jar.

problem_fixes.problem: org.cef cannot be relocated; clashes with other mods shipping org.cef (e.g. MCEF via TeXTech)
problem_fixes.fix: Ship org.cef unrelocated and loaded by the same loader as our OSR class. Startup check: refuse with a message if org.cef.CefApp comes from another jar.

problem_fixes.problem: Late XInitThreads on Linux (window already exists)
problem_fixes.fix: OSR with an external single-threaded pump. libX11 1.8+ is thread-safe by default. If Linux shows X errors at G3, move CefApp.startup to the early-load phase.

problem_fixes.problem: macOS players cannot run CEF under lwjgl3ify (headless AWT, game off the main thread)
problem_fixes.fix: Declared unsupported for 10-25: placeholder 'Telão indisponível no macOS', plus SN2 (labelled safety net). Revisit after the event.

problem_fixes.problem: Platform coverage gaps (Linux LD_LIBRARY_PATH, NixOS, fake arm64, Win7, Pojav)
problem_fixes.fix: Publish the support matrix: Windows 10/11 x64 Tier 1, Linux x64 glibc 2.31+ Tier 2, the rest placeholder. Check the ELF/PE machine type after download.

problem_fixes.problem: Install path, Unicode/space usernames, CWD-relative dirs
problem_fixes.fix: Absolute canonical paths derived from the MC data dir. ASCII-safe fallback (%PROGRAMDATA%\AkashicWeb or the 8.3 short path). Test 'C:\Users\João Conceição' and Prism names with spaces and parentheses.

problem_fixes.problem: Antivirus/firewall/DNS-filter interference
problem_fixes.fix: Download only from Akashic or pinned hosts. A pt-BR guide listing the folder and hashes to whitelist. Detect helper start failure and show AV instructions. Code signing after the event.

problem_fixes.problem: WD/MCEF version coupling and packaging confusion
problem_fixes.fix: One mod jar with the engine version-locked by buildId in the manifest. A clear pt-BR message on mismatch. No auto-download of third-party mods.

problem_fixes.problem: Dedicated server must not load CEF (WD required MCEF on the server)
problem_fixes.fix: All org.cef code in client.web behind proxies and @SideOnly; the TE holds no CEF types. CI boots a dedicated server and places, loads and unloads a screen.

problem_fixes.problem: Legacy WD 0.11 pitfalls (entity screens, configurable IDs, 32-bit, Flash)
problem_fixes.fix: Port from the 1.12.2 TileEntity design only. No configurable IDs. 0.11 is reference only.

problem_fixes.problem: Mod conflicts (Angelica, lwjgl3ify, Hodgepodge in GTNH)
problem_fixes.fix: Test in the exact server pack with Angelica on and off and shaders on and off. Narrow, namespaced mixins. Smoke test after every GTNH update.

problem_fixes.problem: Fork regression: lost range and remote checks; unbounded JSON/text
problem_fixes.fix: Re-add the dimension, 128-block and remote checks, plus per-player rate limits and length caps on URL, text and JSON.

problem_fixes.problem: Security/abuse: unsandboxed Chromium, attacker-chosen URLs, --disable-web-security, exact-host blacklist
problem_fixes.fix: Telão lock plus a server-side UrlPolicy allowlist with isInternal. Client onBeforeBrowse/onBeforeResourceLoad guard. Web security kept on. No popups, downloads, devtools or context menu. AuditLog. CEF kept current.
problem_fixes.source: issues; cef-tech; gtnh-integration; java-cef context.cpp:193-197; AkashicFM UrlPolicy.java:54,153

problem_fixes.problem: Miniserv opens public TCP 25566
problem_fixes.fix: Not ported, neither the server block nor the wd:// scheme. If ever needed, port 0 by default.

problem_fixes.problem: License hygiene (PD WD, MIT fork, LGPL CinemaMod MCEF, no-grant net.montoyo.mcef, jQuery, ironic.ogg)
problem_fixes.fix: Keep the PD headers and credit plus the MIT notice. Do not copy net.montoyo.mcef. CCBlueX java-cef is BSD: keep the LICENSE. Drop ironic.ogg. Record SHA-256 of every native bundle.

problem_fixes.problem: Upstream abandonment (montoyo, CinemaMod)
problem_fixes.fix: A fully owned fork: vendored engine source and our own CI, binaries hosted by Akashic or pinned upstream hashes, no reliance on upstream fixes.

problem_fixes.problem: Retransmission rights and Content ID on the owner's restream
problem_fixes.fix: Source and rights decision: provisional 10-15, final 10-21. Relay only with a licence or permission (TV Câmara CC BY, TV Senado policy, or a broadcaster's written OK); YouTube-only sources via the official embed (backup B). On the owner's stream, mute, blur or switch the telão to the TSE page, and ask the rights holder to allowlist his channel.

problem_fixes.problem: Relay egress bandwidth (~1.9 Mbit/s per viewer at 720p; ~190 Mbit/s for 100)
problem_fixes.fix: MediaMTX on a VPS or the game host with at least 300 Mbit/s egress, a 480p tier, and the browser started only within range. 50-viewer load test at G2.

problem_fixes.problem: WebRTC reachability (UDP 8189, NAT)
problem_fixes.fix: webrtcAdditionalHosts set to the public IP, webrtcLocalTCPAddress enabled, automatic LL-HLS fallback over HTTPS 443, TLS via reverse proxy.

problem_fixes.problem: WebRTC first frame ~3 s (non-trickle ICE wait)
problem_fixes.fix: POST the WHEP offer after the first candidate or 300 ms (or trickle via PATCH). LL-HLS plays first while WebRTC connects.

problem_fixes.problem: Evidence gap: WebRTC VP9/AV1 not run on a no-codec build
problem_fixes.fix: Run the codec-path lat/ harness against both engine variants at G1.

problem_fixes.problem: Expectation of 'almost no ms' delay
problem_fixes.fix: Tell the owner plainly (see latency_answer). Use WebRTC as the primary delivery to minimise our added delay and the skew between players.

problem_fixes.fix: Telão-only MVP, two parallel streams, a dated feature freeze on 10-20, and go/no-go gates with fallbacks at each.

CefNativesInstaller: manifest pinned in the jar, SHA-256 before extract, zip-slip guard, resume/timeouts/mirrors, atomic install under <mcDataDir>/akashic-web, consent prompt, manual-zip import, /telao doctor, preflight report to the server.

Screen block + multiblock (2x2..16x16, raised limit for admin-placed screens), connected-border icons via getIcon, TileEntityScreen with NBT state (URL/preset, resolution fixed 1280x720, rotation, owner, lock flag, source epoch, target delay), sync via getDescriptionPacket/onDataPacket.

macOS support investigation (main-thread CEF vs lwjgl3ify); arm64 builds after verifying binaries.

latency_answer:
Short answer for Gabriel: not "almost no ms" behind the TV, but almost no ms between players. Delay has three separate parts.

(1) Source delay versus the real event. This is set by the broadcaster and cannot be removed by us.
- If the coverage comes from YouTube, Google documents under 10 s for Low latency and under 5 s for Ultra-low latency, with no figure for Normal (VERIFIED, support.google.com/youtube/answer/7444635).
- If OBS captures a TV signal, the TV chain's own delay applies (seconds, INFERRED).

(2) Delay our system adds on top.
- Akashic relay over WebRTC: 126 ms median measured on localhost inside JCEF/Chromium 150 (VERIFIED). Over the internet with capture and encode, about 0.3-0.6 s (INFERRED; gate G2 requires under 1 s).
- Relay over LL-HLS: 1.04 s median on localhost (VERIFIED), about 1.3-2.5 s over the internet (INFERRED; G2 requires under 3 s).
- Direct YouTube embed (codec backup): essentially 0 added, plus each client's own buffering.
- CEF rendering itself: about 33-66 ms (1-2 frames at 30 fps, INFERRED from paint rates).

(3) Difference between players.
- WebRTC: tens of ms. 22 ms was measured between two local clients (VERIFIED); likely up to 100-200 ms across ISPs (INFERRED; G4 requires 150 ms or less).
- LL-HLS: 116 ms measured unsynced (VERIFIED), under about 100-250 ms with server-clock steering (INFERRED; G4 requires 250 ms or less).
- Direct YouTube embed: uncontrolled, likely 1-10 s (INFERRED). This is why the relay is primary.

On his own live channel, his viewers see only his client. Their delay is the total above plus his platform's latency (YouTube Ultra-low under 5 s / Low under 10 s), and differences between players do not matter to them.

Bottom line: on YouTube Ultra-low with our WebRTC relay, expect roughly 3-6 s behind the live event (INFERRED). Expect about 5-11 s if the broadcaster uses Low latency, and more on Normal. Players see the same moment within about a tenth of a second.
open_decisions_for_owner: Freeze the server's GTNH version for the event: 2.8.4 stable (recommended), or 2.9 only if final ships and is certified by about 10-12. Which Java variants to officially support (recommended: both 8 and 17-25).

Source and rights: which coverage to show on 10-25 (a licensed or public broadcaster such as TV Câmara/TV Senado/TV Brasil, a commercial broadcaster with written permission, or a YouTube channel via the official embed only). Who obtains the permission, by when (provisional 10-15, final 10-21).

Codec build: accept distributing or downloading a codec-enabled CEF (OBS 7871, H.264/AAC via FFmpeg; patent grey area, legal input recommended), or ship codec-free CEF 152 and accept that the YouTube-embed backup is unavailable.

Relay hosting and budget: a VPS or the game host with at least 300 Mbit/s egress (or a CDN), and the ingest setup on election night (his PC and uplink of at least 6 Mbit/s, a backup ingest machine, capture card or browser capture).
Staffing: two parallel developers (engine+relay and the WD port) for 15 days, or accept a smaller MVP (no admin keyboard, Windows only).
Admin model: OP level vs an Akashic admin list vs specific UUIDs; whether URL/preset changes during the event need two-person confirmation.
Mod distribution: the mod becomes required in the server pack (block registry). Natives are optional with placeholder, prompted at login with consent, or bundled in the pack download.
Platform stance: officially declare macOS/arm64/Win7 unsupported for 10-25 (placeholder plus SN2 audio relay if rights allow).
Restream policy: on his own channel, mute or blur the telão, switch his view to the TSE page, or obtain allowlisting from the rights holder.
Quality tier: 720p30 default (about 1.9 Mbit/s per viewer) vs 480p default for low-end GTNH clients; whether 1080p opt-in is allowed.
AkashicFM API change (ExternalAudioSources, timed feed) for stage-2 positional audio after the event, given AkashicFM's own release gates.
Naming and credits for the port (Web Displays credit to montoyo/public domain, CinemaMod MIT notice) and the repository where it lives.
